evidence_identity.algorithm: deterministic canonical JSON plus SHA-256 prefix

persistence.storage: embedded in each persisted CausalHypothesis within CausalAnalysisRecord.payload
persistence.late_evidence: creates a new deterministic analysis generation when the evidence input fingerprint changes
persistence.legacy_analysis: ledger remains absent; evidence is not backfilled or fabricated

active_claim_types.known_limitations: Confirms that the selected hypothesis contains a durable change event; it does not prove causation.

active_claim_types.temporal_relevance: authoritative pre-incident effective time supports; authoritative post-incident effective time contradicts; weak authority is explicit missing context
active_claim_types.known_limitations: Temporal precedence is necessary evidence for many change hypotheses but never sufficient proof of causation.

active_claim_types.relationship_relevance: resolved entity can anchor later topology claims
active_claim_types.temporal_relevance: resolution occurs within the pinned snapshot generation
active_claim_types.known_limitations: Ambiguous and unresolved references are missing evidence, never positive evidence and never fuzzy-resolved.

active_claim_types.identity_relevance: uses durable links created by accepted TC-1 correlation
active_claim_types.relationship_relevance: anchors the change to an entity used by the existing 13C path
active_claim_types.temporal_relevance: link is interpreted in the causal analysis generation
active_claim_types.known_limitations: Only exact scope incompatibility or a deterministic resolved-identity versus durable-link conflict is contradiction; absence of a link is not automatically contradiction.

active_claim_types.identity_relevance: path endpoints use canonical topology entity IDs
active_claim_types.relationship_relevance: authoritative path claim over real pinned relationships
active_claim_types.temporal_relevance: always bound to the analysis snapshot, never latest topology
active_claim_types.known_limitations: A missing path is recorded only when a durable change/entity anchor makes the expectation defensible.

active_claim_types.identity_relevance: provenance source references may contain stable provider or object IDs
active_claim_types.relationship_relevance: explains why a relationship exists and which component asserted it
active_claim_types.temporal_relevance: relationship is read only from the pinned analysis snapshot
active_claim_types.known_limitations: Legacy or partial provenance is missing evidence rather than contradiction; TC-4 does not upgrade old relationships.

required_references: signal_id when the incident names a primary signal
active_claim_types.identity_relevance: stable involved entity or provider object identity can anchor the observed failure
active_claim_types.relationship_relevance: none unless already represented in topology
active_claim_types.temporal_relevance: preserves TC-3 signal time without treating receipt time as occurrence
active_claim_types.known_limitations: No missing item is emitted when no signal reference was ever promised; missing is bounded to an explicit unavailable primary signal.

active_claim_types.identity_relevance: immutable digest is direct; mutable tag/reference is limited
active_claim_types.relationship_relevance: uses the real workload-to-artifact relationship in the pinned snapshot
active_claim_types.temporal_relevance: artifact state is bounded to the pinned topology snapshot
active_claim_types.known_limitations: This is evidence explanation, not proof that a build produced an image unless a durable producer reference exists.

active_claim_types.identity_relevance: stable event IDs keep lineage generation-specific
active_claim_types.relationship_relevance: represents the existing selected causal-event edge, not a new graph traversal
active_claim_types.temporal_relevance: lineage events retain their own TC-3 metadata in their other evidence items
active_claim_types.known_limitations: Only lineage already selected by 13C is exposed; TC-4 does not create or rank new lineage edges.
